rics.meaning: China Government Finance: Central Government Balance. Fiscal aggregate or sub-aggregate from MoF.
rics.how_to_use: Track for fiscal-stance signals. China's official deficit (~3% of GDP) understates true fiscal stance — augmented deficit (including LGFVs, special bonds) typically 8-12% of GDP. Watch government fund revenue separately for land-sale revenue impact.

rics.meaning: General Government Expenditure (Budgetary) — central + local government spending. Major lines: education, social security, healthcare, infrastructure, defense, agriculture support, public administration.
rics.how_to_use: Pro-cyclical fiscal stance shifted to counter-cyclical 2018+. Watch the 'special-purpose bond quota' set in March each year — this drives infrastructure spending. Front-loading bond issuance to Q1-Q2 signals counter-cyclical fiscal push.

rics.meaning: General Government Revenue, YoY — pace of revenue growth.
rics.how_to_use: Cyclical with GDP. Watch land-sales-revenue separately reported by MoF — its YoY changes far more cyclical than total revenue.

rics.meaning: General Government Deficit/Surplus — China's official budget balance. Released monthly by the Ministry of Finance.
rics.how_to_use: Official deficit understates true fiscal stance — excludes local-government financing vehicles (LGFVs), special bonds, and other off-budget items. Augmented fiscal deficit (IMF measure) typically 8-12% of GDP vs official ~3%. Watch the official-vs-augmented gap.

rics.meaning: General Government Revenue — central + local tax + non-tax receipts. Major sources: VAT (~40%), corporate income tax (~25%), individual income tax (~7%), customs (~3%), state-owned-enterprise dividends (~7%).
rics.how_to_use: Tax-to-GDP ~16% — moderate. Land sales (counted separately as 'government fund revenue', ~CNY 8 trillion historical peak) are critical to local-government finances; collapsed 2022-24 with property downturn — major fiscal stress point.

rics.meaning: Central Government Deficit/Surplus (Standardized) — central-only fiscal balance (excludes local governments). The 'on-budget' deficit subject to the 3%-of-GDP cap.
rics.how_to_use: Used in central-government budget arithmetic. Local-government deficits run ~4-6% of GDP separately, financed via LGFV bonds and special-purpose bonds. The total 'general government' framework is the meaningful sustainability measure.
